Thunder Bluff (sometimes spelled as Thunderbluff) is the tauren capital city located in the northern part of the region of Mulgore on the continent of Kalimdor. The entire city is built on bluffs several hundred feet above the surrounding landscape and is accessible by elevators on the southwestern and northeastern sides. Established by the wise chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof and his stalwart tribe, Thunder Bluff overlooks the verdant land of Mulgore from atop a series of windswept mesas. Prior to the construction of the capital, the tauren had lived as nomads for countless generations, often under attack by marauding bands of centaur. With Thunder Bluff’s founding, however, the proud and good-spirited race was finally granted a permanent home.
The city of many tribes is a hub for tauren, welcoming tradesfolk and artisans of every kind.

Honor them, and in doing so honor yourself.|{{NPC||Baine Bloodhoof||High Chieftain Baine Bloodhoof}}}} '''Thunder Bluff''' (sometimes spelled as '''Thunderbluff''')[[A Fair Trade (Orgrimmar)]][[Sacred Fire]][[Stay of Execution]]''[[Shadows Rising]]'', pg. 20, 110, 139 is the [[tauren]] capital [[city]] located in the northern part of the region of [[Mulgore]] on the continent of [[Kalimdor]]. The entire city is built on bluffs several hundred feet above the surrounding landscape and is accessible by elevators on the southwestern and northeastern sides. Established by the wise chieftain [[Cairne Bloodhoof]] and his stalwart tribe, Thunder Bluff overlooks the verdant land of [[Mulgore]] from atop a series of windswept mesas. Prior to the construction of the capital, the tauren had lived as nomads for countless generations, often under attack by marauding bands of [[centaur]]. With Thunder Bluff’s founding, however, the proud and good-spirited race was finally granted a permanent home. The city of many tribes is a hub for tauren, welcoming tradesfolk and artisans of every kind.''[[World of Warcraft: Exploring Azeroth: Kalimdor]]'', pg. 84 {{OTOC|550|207}} ==History== ===Founding=== {{WC3-section}} During the [[Third War]] in 21 [[ADP]], [[Cairne Bloodhoof|Cairne]] and his [[Bloodhoof tribe]] received help from [[Warchief]] [[Thrall]] and the [[New Horde]], and were eventually able to drive back the [[centaur]] and claim the grasslands of [[Mulgore]] for their own. For the first time in hundreds of years, the tauren had a land to call their own. Upon the windswept mesa of Thunder Bluff, Cairne built a refuge for his people, where tauren of every tribe are welcome. Over time, the scattered tauren tribes united under Cairne's rule. There are a few tribes who disagree about the direction their new nation should take, but all agree that Cairne is the wisest and best suited to lead them towards the future. After the [[Battle of Mount Hyjal]], [[Rexxar]] and his companions were tasked by [[Tagar (tauren)|Tagar]] with driving the [[Stonetalon Mountains|Stonetalon]] [[Harpy|harpies]] away from the tauren's [[kodo]] herds, for the foul creatures were slaughtering them and leaving their bodies to rot. Mulgore was also home to a large group of [[centaur]], who had captured [[Baine Bloodhoof]] and thrown his father Cairne into despair. With the help of [[Bovan Windtotem]], Rexxar rescued Baine and brought the tauren back into the [[Horde]].[[Old Hatreds (WC3 Orc)]] ===World of Warcraft=== {{wow-section}} [[File:Thunder Bluff Cataclysm.jpg|thumb|Thunder Bluff in ''World of Warcraft''.]] The city of Thunder Bluff lies atop a series of mesas that overlook the verdant grasslands of Mulgore. Once a nomadic people, the tauren recently established the city as a center for trade caravans, traveling artisans, and inventors of every kind. The proud city also stands as a refuge for the many hunters who stalk their dangerous prey through the Barrens and its surrounding areas. Long bridges of wood and rope span the chasms between the mesas, and each mesa is topped with tents, longhouses, colorfully painted totems, and spirit lodges. The mighty chief, Cairne Bloodhoof, presides over the bustling city, ensuring that the united tauren tribes live in peace and security.''[[World of Warcraft: Game Manual]]'', pg. 183 In order to gain access to Thunder Bluff, visitors must either ride [[wyvern]]s to the top of one of the four towering mesas, use the zeppelin from [[Orgrimmar]] or be lifted via rope and wood elevators from the foot of the bluffs, an invention unique to the tauren. ===The Comic=== {{comic-section}} [[File:thunderbluffcomic.jpg|thumb|Thunder Bluff as seen in ''[[World of Warcraft: The Comic|The Comic]]''.]] Prior to the [[war against the Lich King]], Thunder Bluff's [[Pools of Vision]] became haunted by an element rumored to be summoned by [[Magatha Grimtotem]]. The city was later visited by [[Rehgar Earthfury]] and his two gladiators - [[Broll]] and [[Lo'Gosh]] who destroyed the element and eventually escaped from [[slavery]].''[[World of Warcraft: The Comic]]'' - Issue 3: ''[[Destiny Awaits!]]'' A human assassin from the [[Stormwind Assassin's Guild]] also visited Magatha in order to learn the location of Lo'Gosh.''[[World of Warcraft: The Comic]]'' - Issue 4: ''[[Balancing the Scales (comic)|Balancing the Scales]]'' ===Stormrage=== {{novel-section}} During the [[War Against the Nightmare]] in 27 ADP, Thunder Bluff was enveloped by the mists of the [[Emerald Nightmare]], but [[Malfurion Stormrage]] was able to find Baine in the city and recruit him into the [[dreamform army]].''[[Stormrage]]'', chapter 24 ===Elemental Unrest=== {{wotlk-section}} During the [[Elemental Unrest]], the city was attacked by furious water and wind [[elemental]]s, until [[Baine Bloodhoof]] and his forces repelled them with the [[Horde]] [[adventurer]]s. ===The Shattering=== {{Novel-section}} {{For|the battle for Thunder Bluff|Battle for Thunder Bluff}} Following Cairne's death in a duel with [[Warchief]] [[Garrosh Hellscream]], Thunder Bluff was briefly seized in a coup by [[Magatha Grimtotem]] and elements of her tribe. The capital was later assaulted by the [[Grimtotem tribe|Grimtotem]] [[assassin]]s who mainly targeted experts in weapons, powerful [[druid]]s, or [[shaman]]. They also slaughtered the [[Skychaser tribe]] at the [[Spirit Rise]], killed many hunters at the [[Hunter Rise]], and even some others who could lift a weapon only to strike fear into the remaining tauren. Only the [[Forsaken]] were spared from casualties since they were supporting the Grimtotem. Thanks to the efforts of [[Jevan Grimtotem]] and [[Jaina Proudmoore]], Baine was eventually able to rally an army and buy weapons needed to defeat the Grimtotem. In retaliation, Baine launched a brilliant counterattack using a fleet of zeppelins. After he strategically divided Magatha's forces, Thunder Bluff was recaptured, and Baine assumed his role as the high chieftain of the tauren tribes. In the aftermath, Magatha and her loyalists were sent to exile, while Jevan became the leader of the Grimtotem who remained with the Horde and Thunder Bluff.''[[The Shattering: Prelude to Cataclysm]]'' ===Cataclysm=== {{cata-section}} [[File:Thunder Bluff in the distance.jpg|thumb|Thunder Bluff after the [[Cataclysm (event)|Cataclysm]].]] Following the [[Cataclysm (event)|Cataclysm]] in 28 ADP, having recovered from the recent unrest, the capital was once again a bastion of peace and security for Kalimdor's tauren. As a [[shaman]]istic tribe, the [[Cloudsong tribe]] replaced the murdered Skychaser tribe. When the [[Camp Taurajo]] fell, Baine had a gate separating the Barrens and Mulgore constructed. Some tauren were content with that decision and did not burn for revenge, but the Grimtotem who disagreed, and others who chose to strike back at the Alliance from Vendetta Point, were expelled from Thunder Bluff, though suffered no other repercussions.''[[Jaina Proudmoore: Tides of War]]'', pg. 29 (ebook) ===Legion=== {{Legion-section}} During the [[third invasion of the Burning Legion]] in 32 ADP, Thunder Bluff was under attack by [[infernal]]s, which were eventually destroyed by the [[Earthen Ring]].[[A Ring Unbroken]] Thunder Bluff also appeared in the [[Emerald Nightmare (instance)|Emerald Nightmare]] with the rises being shattered and the city floating on its side. ===Before the Storm=== {{Novel-section}} After the [[Argus Campaign]] and the [[Orgrimmar]] parade, Thunder Bluff hosted [[Warchief]] [[Sylvanas Windrunner]] and several representatives of other Horde races to speak about the tragedy in [[Silithus]] on the behest of [[Archdruid Hamuul Runetotem]]. Soon after, they were joined by [[Magni Bronzebeard]] who warned the Horde about the injuries of [[Azeroth (titan)|Azeroth]].''[[Before the Storm]]'', chapter 12 ===Thunder Bluff's feast=== {{bfa-section}} [[File:Highmountain Pathfinders Thunder Bluff.jpg|thumb|[[Highmountain Pathfinder]]s in Thunder Bluff.]] Prior to the [[Fourth War]], Thunder Bluff held a feast for the [[Highmountain tauren]] from [[Highmountain]] on the [[Broken Shore]]. The whole city was celebrating with fireworks until it was attacked by [[Uul'gyneth]] who sensed [[Spiritwalker Ebonhorn]] having left Highmountain and thus the protection of the wards. They trapped the city civilians with the void power turning them unresponsive. The city was defended by Horde adventurers, Baine Bloodhoof, his personal guards, as well as the city guards who killed the void minions and their leader, [[Qy'telek]].[[A Feast for Our Kin]][[Shadow Over Thunder Bluff]][[Dark Forces]] File:Thunder Bluff feast 1.jpg|Thunder Bluff feast. File:Thunder Bluff feast 2.jpg File:Thunder Bluff feast 3.jpg File:Thunder Bluff feast 4.jpg File:Thunder Bluff feast 5.jpg|A drinking [[Bluffwatcher]]. ===Battle for Azeroth=== {{Bfa-section}} [[File:Thunder Bluff during battle at the Gates of Orgrimmar.jpg|thumb|Thunder Bluff during the [[Battle at the Gates of Orgrimmar|battle at Orgrimmar]].]] During the course of the [[Fourth War]] in 33 ADP, tauren [[warbrave]]s were sent from the city into the [[Barrens]].[[Great Gate of Mulgore (Alliance)]] [[Alliance]] champions were sent to hold them at the [[Great Gate]] of [[Mulgore]] and encountered [[Kary Thunderhorn]] among them at the [[Ruins of Taurajo]].[[Great Gate of Mulgore (Alliance)]] After Baine was rescued from the [[Underhold]] by [[Thrall]] and [[Jaina Proudmoore]], they feared [[Sylvanas Windrunner]] would burn Thunder Bluff like she did [[Teldrassil]].[[Stay of Execution]] Baine later called for tauren champions who had proven their worth to return at Thunder Bluff at once, for the [[spiritwalker]]s had whispered their name with urgency.[[When Spirits Whisper]] When Thunder Bluff came under attack by a [[Malevolent Spirit]] from the [[Shadowlands]], Baine rallied the tauren forces in defending the city.[[Answer the Call]] By the end of the war, the citizens of Thunder Bluff supported [[Varok Saurfang]] in his revolution against Sylvanas, though Baine's wounds would force him to remain within the city rather than march to [[Orgrimmar]]. In case the Banshee Queen would launch a counterattack, [[Ji Firepaw]], [[Aysa Cloudsinger]], [[Mayla Highmountain]], and their forces reinforced the city's defenses.[[Strategic Deployment]] After the [[battle at the Gates of Orgrimmar]], during which Saurfang died in [[mak'gora]] against Sylvanas to a [[Mak'gora]], a stunned [[Lor'themar Theron|Lor'themar]] ordered for [[Adventurer|champions]] to report what had transpired to Baine. With Thunder Bluff no longer under the threat of an attack, the reinforcements left the city as Baine, Ji, and Mayla traveled to Orgrimmar to attend the funeral of Saurfang.[[The Price of Victory]] ===Shadowlands=== {{Shadowlands-section}} In Year 35 ADP, [[Baine Bloodhoof]] and [[Mayla Highmountain]] were in the city when the [[Mawsworn]] attacked and captured Baine.[[Cause for Distraction]] ==Geography== Thunder Bluff is located in the far north of Mulgore, among the sprawling flatlands of the [[Golden Plains]]. The city is composed of four towering mesas or rises. The only entrances from the plains below are elevators leading to the central platform. The central rise is connected to the others through large wooden bridges. ===Rises=== [[File:WorldMap-ThunderBluff.jpg|thumb|Map of Thunder Bluff.]] The various rises in Thunder Bluff act a bit like neighborhoods or quarters in a human city, or the valleys and keeps of the orcish city [[Orgrimmar]]. Thunder Bluff has a central mesa divided into three rises, surrounded by three additional mesas with distinct names: *'''[[Central mesa]]''' - In the game is split into the lower rise, the middle rise, and the high rise. **'''[[Lower rise]]''' - Located near the southwestern lifts from the main north road. **'''[[Middle rise]]''' - Located near the northeastern lifts from the plains. **'''[[High Rise]]''' - Located east from the wind rider roost. *'''[[Elder Rise]]''' - Located across the rope bridges from the middle or the high rise. *'''[[Hunter Rise]]''' - Located across the rope bridges from lower and high rise. *'''[[Spirit Rise]]''' - Located across the rope bridges from lower and middle rise. **'''[[Pools of Vision|The Pools of Vision]]''' - The cave entrance is found in the Spirit Rise. ===Points of interest=== {{main|Thunder Bluff points of interest}} *The [[Bank]] is on the southeastern side of the Lower rise. *The top of the [[Wind Rider Roost]] in the central totem pole houses [[Wind Rider]] Master [[Tal]], the [[Flight master]], and [[Brave Tuho]], the Thunder Bluff [[Quartermaster]]. *The [[inn]] is on the southern part of the lower rise. *The [[Auction House]] is located on the lower rise, just west of the entrance to the wind rider roost. *The [[mailbox]] is located just outside the bank. (There's only one mailbox in TB.) *The fishing hole is located in the center of the lower rise. *The [[zeppelin]] dock is located on the west of Spirit Rise. ===Other locations=== *[[Goblin Bazaar]] {{WC3-inline}} ==Notable characters== {{main|Thunder Bluff NPCs}} [[File:Glowei Baine Bloodhoof.jpg|thumb|[[Baine Bloodhoof]], High Chieftain of the Tauren.]] The new Chief of the Bloodhoof clan, [[Baine Bloodhoof]] has become the High Chieftain of the tauren race in wake of his father's death. He watches over Thunder Bluff, and over his people in an ever-darkening world. Baine can be found in the chieftain's tent in the eastern main city and is accompanied by his Honor Guards. [[Hamuul Runetotem]] is the elder druid of Thunder Bluff, and a childhood friend of Cairne. Although he at one point left to fight on [[Mount Hyjal]], he can always be found on [[Elder Rise]]. ==Travel connections== ===Flight=== ;{{Horde}} [[Orgrimmar]] ;{{Horde}} [[Sun Rock Retreat]] ;{{Horde}} [[The Crossroads]] ;{{Horde}} [[Shadowprey Village]] ;{{Horde}} [[Brackenwall Village]] ;{{Horde}} [[Camp Mojache]] ;{{Horde}} [[Freewind Post]] ;{{Neutral}} [[Gadgetzan]] ===Zeppelin=== ;{{Horde}} [[Orgrimmar]] ==In the RPG== {{RPG-section}} ===History=== The [[centaur]] were driving the tauren out of their homeland around the time of the [[Third War]]. When [[Thrall]] and his Horde arrived on the [[continent]], an alliance was forged between the Horde and the tauren. Following the defeat of [[Archimonde]] and the end of the war, Thrall helped the tauren rout the centaur and reclaim their land. Shortly thereafter the tauren founded the city of Thunder Bluff and began the process of settling into their old surroundings and repairing the ecological damage the centaur had wrought. Thunder Bluff grows and expands at a tremendous rate.''[[Lands of Mystery]]'', pg. 48 The city was described as being built atop a near-impenetrable mesa deep in the south of Mulgore.''[[Warcraft: The Roleplaying Game]]'', pg. 207 The weather is almost always warm and sunny, with intermittent breezes carried in from The Barrens.''[[Lands of Mystery]]'', pg. 47 ===People and culture=== Although some of the historically nomadic tauren probably miss their itinerant lifestyle, they are intensely proud of their permanent home and spend much of their time trying to make it better. They gladly accept the help of the [[orc]]s and [[troll]]s that help them, but are somewhat less enthusiastic at the presence of the [[Forsaken]], whom they only grudgingly tolerate because of their membership in the Horde. Tauren place a strong emphasis on the value of life, and the unlife of the Forsaken stands as an affront to their beliefs,''[[Lands of Mystery]]'', pg. 46 - 47 not to mention the less than honorable activities the Forsaken carry out. ==Notes and trivia== [[File:Thunder Bluff card back.png|thumb|200px|A card back themed after Thunder Bluff in ''[[Hearthstone (game)|Hearthstone]]''.]] *At some point, Thunder Bluff was caught ablaze.''[[Jaina Proudmoore: Tides of War]]'', pg. 222 (ebook) *[[Galena Stormspear]]'s mother has a tavern in the city.''[[Traveler: The Shining Blade]]'', chapter 10 *Occasionally, some [[Darkspear tribe|Darkspear]] [[jungle troll|trolls]] travel to Thunder Bluff to live with the tauren and adopt their ways. [[Chen Stormstout]] refers to these trolls as "blue tauren".''[[Vol'jin: Shadows of the Horde]]'', pg. 36, 100 *Thunder Bluff's elevators and windmills are kept in working order by [[Engineer Palehoof]].[[Bluffwatcher#Quotes]] *The diamond [[Magni Bronzebeard]] was so heavy that the lifts were not able to carry him.''[[Before the Storm]]'', chapter 12 *Daily fishing and cooking quests that give [[Thunder Bluff (faction)|Thunder Bluff]] [[reputation]] are offered from [[Kah Mistrunner]] and [[Aska Mistrunner]] on the [[High Rise]]. *It's a bad idea to jump from the top of one of the bluffs, as the fall is generally fatal without some sort of slowing effect. If you want to save time, you can jump on the platform under the main elevators. The fall damage may not kill you, but will reduce your health significantly. **[[Sunwalker Dezco]] claims to have fallen off the Thunder Bluff elevators on more than one occasion.[[Herbal Remedies]] *Thunder Bluff is most likely the optimal place for flying in Kalimdor for the Horde, as it is located in almost the center of the continent. *Thunder Bluff is the only capital city in which player [[duel]]s are permitted, becoming available when within the Hunter Rise. *Strangely, while ''[[The Shattering: Prelude to Cataclysm]]'' describes "hundreds of corpses" in the city after the [[battle for Thunder Bluff]], the only in-game change the city received in ''[[World of Warcraft: Cataclysm|Cataclysm]]'' was the replacement of the [[Skychaser tribe|Skychasers]], most of whom were killed during the events of the novel. *Thunder Bluff is [[Thunder Bluff (Drums of War)|a Rare Location card]] in the ''[[World of Warcraft: Trading Card Game]]'''s [[Drums of War (TCG)|Drums of War]] set. *In {{g|hs}}, the Thunder Bluff {{HS|card back}} was rewarded for achieving Rank 20 in Ranked Season 23, which took place during February 2016. The flavor text reads: ''"Unofficial slogan: "Great warriors come from happy Tauren tribes. Happy Tauren come from Thunder Bluff!""'' *During the development of the original ''World of Warcraft'', Thunder Bluff was one of the easiest racial capital cities to create, taking about two weeks of modeling.{{Ref web|url=https://countdowntoclassic.com/2018/08/20/episode-63-the-making-of-world-of-warcraft-with-vanilla-dev-john-staats/|title=Countdown To Classic: Episode #63 – The Making Of World Of Warcraft With Vanilla Dev, John Staats (around 2:28:20)|date=2018-08-20|accessdate=2018-09-24}} ==Gallery== File:ThunderbluffCraigSymonds.jpg|Thunder Bluff's skyline as seen from [[Mulgore]].
